paragraphs: In Dundee you can foster with Dundee City Council's Fostering and Adoption service or with one of the independent agencies listed above; the Care Inspectorate keeps a directory of registered fostering services in Scotland. The council says it especially needs carers for groups of brothers and sisters and for children and young people with additional needs, as well as for babies and toddlers.

The city offers a wide range of fostering: emergency care for a few nights; short breaks at weekends or in the holidays, including for children who live with their own families; interim care lasting from weeks up to two years; long-term care; and permanent care until at least 18. You need to be over 21 to foster with the council, in good health and with a spare bedroom; there is no upper age limit and no qualifications are required.

Unusually, Dundee publishes its rates. Its table, dated from April 2024, shows a weekly allowance for each child rising with age from £177.68 for under-fives to £283.35 for 16 to 18 year olds, plus a carer fee of £271.74 a week per child, a holiday allowance and extra payments at birthdays, in the summer and at Christmas. Carers are self-employed for tax and must register with HMRC. Ask the council to confirm today's rates when you enquire.

Approved carers get a named social worker, free training and support groups, a 24-hour out-of-hours service, help with start-up costs and equipment, and 21 days of paid leave a year. The council says assessment takes up to six months; the Scottish Government's guide says six to twelve months is typical, ending with a fostering panel. Speak to the council and two or three services above, and see the Fife page if you live across the Tay.

sources.title: Dundee Fostering and Adoption (Dundee City Council)
